context_for_next_agent: CONTINUES 20260813-0702, whose only blocker was 'Docker down, blocks migration and concurrency verification'. That is now CLOSED, and the verification it unlocked found two real defects. DOCKER IS STILL DOWN: com.docker.service is Stopped and needs an elevated UAC click; the user was on a phone and could not click it, and UAC must not be worked around. It did not matter — the work needed Postgres on localhost:5432, not Docker, and WSL Ubuntu already ships PostgreSQL 16 at /usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin. sudo there wants a password so systemctl is out, but Postgres needs no root: initdb + pg_ctl as the normal user, data dir on WSL-native fs (NEVER /mnt/d — 9p reports 0777 and cannot chmod, initdb demands 0700), socket dir overridden with -k because /var/run/postgresql is not writable. That reproduces docker-compose's postgres:password@localhost:5432/skn_app_db exactly. Also: invoke wsl from the PowerShell tool, not Bash — Git Bash mangles /mnt/... args into Windows paths. MIGRATION IS NOW VERIFIED FOR REAL against an empty DB, so the whole ~55-revision chain ran: upgrade head clean to e6f7g8h9i0j1; `alembic check --target local` = 'No new upgrade operations detected'; downgrade -1 drops exactly its own 6 columns + ix_bookings_slot + ix_bookings_reminder_due while leaving bookings_pkey, ix_bookings_id and ix_bookings_queue_number (owned by 1349087a4a24) intact; re-upgrade restores; check clean again. THE CONCURRENCY TESTS HAD NEVER EXECUTED ONCE — the previous checkpoint recorded '4 skipped by design', which was wrong, and TWO defects were hiding behind that skip. (1) pytest.ini sets only testpaths, so pytest-asyncio runs STRICT, where @pytest.mark.asyncio covers test functions but an async FIXTURE must be @pytest_asyncio.fixture; `sessions` was a plain @pytest.fixture and errored at setup under pytest 9. It is the first async fixture in the whole backend suite, which is why nothing had hit the rule before. Fixed at the fixture, NOT by setting asyncio_mode=auto (that would change collection for ~930 tests to fix one file). (2) with the fixture working, both racers got the same user_id from _any_user_id(), and create_booking checks the duplicate guard BEFORE capacity, so the loser returned DuplicateBookingError and the oversell path was never entered. Fixed per the user's explicit choice: the fixture now creates the two bookers it races (booking-race-a/-b) and deletes them again, which also removed the 'no users seeded' skip — the file now runs on an empty CI database with no preconditions. Result 4 passed, 0 skipped. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN, and this is the part to trust: a green concurrency test proves nothing by itself because it looks identical whether it caught a race or the tasks never overlapped. Temporarily disabling pg_advisory_xact_lock made both oversell tests fail, with 'duplicate queue number issued: [260817-001, 260817-001]' — both invariants the day-scoped lock protects broke together, exactly as designed. booking_service.py was restored with git checkout -- and confirmed by an empty git diff HEAD. TEST BASELINE MOVED: full backend suite is now 870 passed / 0 failed / 60 errors, up from 761. The 60 errors did not vanish, they CHANGED CAUSE — now 'Redis at 127.0.0.1:6379 not reachable' instead of 'PostgreSQL not reachable'; those tests need both and were dying at the first gate. All 8 affected files are live-chat/websocket/auth (test_websocket, test_session_claim, test_reconnection, test_cookie_auth, test_liff_token, test_multi_operator, test_operator_takeover, test_conversation_preferences) and NO booking file is among them; `-k booking` is 131 passed, 0 skipped. Redis is not installed in WSL and apt needs the sudo password, so that gap stays open locally. CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS CHECKLIST, do not repeat it: it said to confirm `alembic check --target remote` prints 'No new upgrade operations detected' BEFORE opening the PR. That is impossible — alembic check refuses to compare unless the DB is already at head, and PROD sits at d5e6f7g8h9i0 with the booking migration unapplied, so it returns 'Target database is not up to date. FAILED', which says nothing about drift. It is a POST-deploy check; the pre-PR equivalent is --target local after upgrade head. PROD was read only, never written. The only source change this session is backend/tests/test_booking_create_concurrency.py; the 7 feature commits from last session are untouched and nothing has been pushed.
